source.title: BranchNorm: Robustly Scaling Extremely Deep Transformers
source.authors: Yanjun Liu; Xian-Feng Zeng; Fan-Dong Meng; Jie Zhou

record.tranche_reason: Tests deep-training stability and convergence in extremely deep Transformer translation models, extending the depth and shortcut discussion to a different architecture and task.
record.gate_note: The study reports translation BLEU and whether training diverged, not training classification error. Table results for other methods are included only where they compare the deep-training behavior named in V3. Cited findings from prior work and figure-only training curves are not extracted as independent results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates residual Transformers using dynamic branch scaling, translation BLEU, gradient norms and training stability. It does not compare plain convolutional networks with identity-shortcut counterparts as V3 requires. It also does not isolate initialization effects, batch normalization or stability-threshold learning rates. Its own results therefore test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that BranchNorm smooths early training gradients and then returns to standard Post-LN, improving the trade-off between training stability and convergence performance relative to DeepNorm on translation tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Dynamically scales the non-residual Transformer branch during early training and then decays to Post-LN; tests translation BLEU and divergence rather than classification training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Model depth and translation dataset affect reported BLEU and divergence; BranchNorm is described as insensitive to T and more tolerant of warmup and larger learning rates than DeepNorm. Values in the associated plots are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: BranchNorm dynamically increases the non-residual branch multiplier to one, reports smoother early gradients, and subsequently achieves faster convergence and higher translation BLEU than DeepNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic early branch scaling can improve the stability and subsequent translation performance of extremely deep Post-LN Transformers relative to fixed DeepNorm scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.1 reports stable training of a 200-layer BranchNorm Transformer without warmup and better tolerance of larger learning rates than DeepNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BranchNorm improves warmup and learning-rate robustness of deep residual Transformers relative to DeepNorm.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors attribute declining deep-model BLEU on smaller datasets provisionally to overfitting, while larger datasets benefit from depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The translation-quality benefit of increasing Transformer depth depends on dataset scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study reports translation BLEU rather than training classification error. Some comparisons are directly cited from prior papers; DeepNorm is reimplemented. Several training-curve and hyperparameter results are only shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 multilingual task results, Figures 3–9, and other method rows from Tables 1–2 were not extracted. Table 3 reports aggregate translation BLEU for additional models/depths; figures include gradient norms, training curves, hyperparameter sensitivity, representation similarity and sparsity. The study's textual descriptions of these are summarized in gate_note or method_sensitivity, but they do not report the training classification error in V3.

untested.parts: All: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR, including random labels and capacity or training-recipe effects.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
All: depth-related training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs, the matched identity-shortcut comparison, longer training, and the specified plain-tanh and Fixup exceptions.

All: isolated initialization comparisons establishing learning-speed or trainable-depth effects. The experiments follow DeepNorm initialization rather than varying initialization while holding the architecture and training method fixed.
All: initial linearized stability limits, catapult dynamics, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability sharpness trajectories. Larger-learning-rate tolerance alone does not test these.
All: batch normalization versus its absence and Fixup's normalization-free residual training. LayerNorm and branch scaling are different interventions.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V3 verdicts. Residual-Transformer divergence is not evidence for the specified plain-CNN versus shortcut claim, and an untested training-error outcome cannot justify limits_scope. All corrected states concern applicability to V1–V6, not whether the reported translation results occurred. Table 2's flattened layout leaves several subject/value assignments uncertain. Figures 3–9 and Table 3 are already declared in rows_left_out; no omitted result testing a supplied version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima and student width.

Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, ImageNet and CIFAR-10 training error, longer training comparisons, and the specific comparison of identity shortcuts. The study instead tests Post-LN Transformers on translation BLEU and reports divergence and convergence.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation comparisons across initialization types, tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, squared loss, curvature or sharpness changes, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, and Fixup without normalization.

relation.reason: It discusses initialization, gradients, residual connections and deep-network optimization, without testing the specific systems, comparisons or effects in V1–V6.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates dynamic residual-Transformer branch scaling, translation BLEU and stability. It neither tests a claim version nor uses a version's finding as an established tool.

source_check.notes: Table 2 loses row and column alignment where several requested assignments matter. The authors' conclusion about early gradient stability followed by improved convergence is accurately paraphrased; cannot_determine is appropriate for these rows.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Post-LN Transformers on WMT-17 En-De at 18L-18L, 50L-50L, 100L-100L and 250L-250L
reader_labels.reason: Vanilla Post-LN is reported to diverge in most cases at these depths (R2–R5). The task metric is BLEU and divergence, not training error.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: BranchNorm and DeepNorm Transformers on WMT-17 En-De and WMT-14 En-Fr
reader_labels.reason: The tested deep models report BLEU scores and convergence comparisons, so these results do not establish the version's training-error outcome (R6–R15, R22–R32).
